1) Rule implementation - File: src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Exposes ESLint rule `valid-story-reference` that scans all comments for lines starting with `@story` and parses the path from each line (function `handleComment` → `validateStoryPath` → `processStoryPath`). - Uses `const cwd = (context as any).cwd ?? process.cwd();` and configured `storyDirectories` to resolve paths, satisfying REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION and integration with prior annotation-format validation. - Security checks (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION): - Rejects absolute paths when `allowAbsolutePaths` is false via `path.isAbsolute(storyPath)` and `invalidPath` reports. - Uses `containsPathTraversal(storyPath)` plus `path.resolve(cwd, storyPath)` and a `startsWith(cwd + path.sep)` check to block traversal outside project, reporting `invalidPath`. - Extension enforcement (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION): when `requireExt` is true and `!hasValidExtension(storyPath)`, reports `invalidExtension` with the offending `path`. - Existence & error handling (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING): - Delegates to `normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs)` and `reportExistenceProblems`. - `reportExistenceStatus` distinguishes `missing` → `fileMissing` and `fs-error` → `fileAccessError` including a normalized error message in `data.error`. - Project boundary enforcement (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY): - `handleProjectBoundaryForExistence` and `analyzeCandidateBoundaries` call `enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd)` and: - If all candidates are outside project → report `invalidPath` and stop. - If an `exists` result’s `matchedPath` is outside project → report `invalidPath`. - Configurability (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS): meta.schema supports `storyDirectories: string[]`, `allowAbsolutePaths: boolean`, `requireStoryExtension: boolean`; `create` reads these options and passes them into validation. - User-facing messages (User Experience): `fileMissing`, `invalidExtension`, `invalidPath`, and `fileAccessError` provide specific, human-readable diagnostics that include the offending `{{path}}` (and `{{error}}` for filesystem problems). - Inline `@story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md` and `@req` tags link this implementation directly to this story and its requirements.
2) Utilities for path resolution, existence, security, caching, and boundaries - File: src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - Path resolution & candidates (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS): - `buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs)`: - For `./` or `../` paths, resolves once against `cwd`. - For bare paths, resolves under `cwd` and then under each configured `storyDirectories` directory, using `path.basename(storyPath)`. - Project boundary (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY): - `enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd)` computes normalized absolute paths and returns `{ candidate, isWithinProject }`, where `isWithinProject` only if path equals cwd or starts with `cwd + path.sep`. - Caching & performance (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION): - `fileExistStatusCache: Map` caches existence checks per-absolute-path. - `checkSingleCandidate` consults the cache first; on miss it runs file system checks and stores the result. - `__resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests()` clears cache for repeatable tests. - Robust file existence & error handling (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING): - `checkSingleCandidate(candidate)` wraps `fs.existsSync` and `fs.statSync` in try/catch, returning: - `{ status: "missing" }` when the path doesn’t exist or isn’t a regular file. - `{ status: "exists" }` when `stat.isFile()` is true. - `{ status: "fs-error", error }` when any filesystem call throws; it never rethrows. - `getStoryExistence(candidates)` iterates candidates and returns: - `status: "exists"` with `matchedPath` on first success. - Else, if any candidate had `fs-error`, returns `status: "fs-error"` with a representative `error`. - Else returns `status: "missing"`. - `storyExists(paths)` wraps `getStoryExistence` and returns a boolean (`status === "exists"`), preserving the older API while leveraging better error semantics. - `normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs)` calls `buildStoryCandidates` and `getStoryExistence` and returns `{ candidates, exists, existence }`. - Security helpers (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION): - `isAbsolutePath`, `containsPathTraversal`, `isTraversalUnsafe`, `hasValidExtension`, `isUnsafeStoryPath` encapsulate checks for absolute paths, `..` segments, and enforced `.story.md` extension. - All key functions are annotated with `@story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md` and the relevant `@req` IDs, explicitly tying them to this story’s requirements.

expects `invalidPath`. - `relaxedExtensionTester`: - With `requireStoryExtension: false` and `storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"]`, accepts `.story.md` references and ensures no false `invalidExtension` when extension checks are disabled. - Project boundary tests (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY): - `projectBoundaryTester` invalid case uses an absolute path under a directory rooted at `path.resolve(path.sep, "outside-project")` with `allowAbsolutePaths: true` and `storyDirectories: [that outside path]` and expects `invalidPath`, demonstrating that even misconfigured external storyDirectories do not permit out-of-project files. - Additional Jest-based configuration and boundary tests: - After-each cleans temporary dirs, resets existence cache, and restores Jest mocks. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] uses storyDirectories when resolving relative paths`: mocks `fs.existsSync`/`fs.statSync` so only `docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` is treated as existing; `runRuleOnCode("// @story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md", [{ storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"] }])` verifies resolution uses `storyDirectories` and does not crash. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] allowAbsolutePaths permits absolute paths inside project when enabled`: constructs absolute path under project, runs with `allowAbsolutePaths: true`, ensures diagnostics are collected without error. - `[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] storyDirectories cannot escape project even when normalize resolves outside cwd`: uses `// @story ../outside-boundary.story.md` plus in-project reference and checks diagnostics flow, exercising traversal and boundary logic. - `[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] misconfigured storyDirectories outside project cannot validate external files`: mocks filesystem to make only an external path like `/tmp/outside/external-story.story.md` exist; with `allowAbsolutePaths: true` and `storyDirectories: [outsideDir]`, confirms diagnostics include at least one `invalidPath` (enforcing project boundaries against misconfiguration). - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] requireStoryExtension=false accepts existing .md story file`: mocks `docs/stories/developer-story.map.md` as existing and, with `requireStoryExtension: false`, verifies no `invalidExtension` diagnostics (extension relax behavior). - Error handling tests (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING): - `[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] storyExists returns false when fs throws`: mocks `fs.existsSync` and `fs.statSync` to throw EACCES; `storyExists([...])` is asserted not to throw and to return `false`. - `[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] storyExists returns false when fs.statSync throws EIO and existsSync is true`: ensures `getStoryExistence` and `storyExists` handle IO errors and still return `false` without exceptions. - `[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] rule reports fileAccessError when fs.statSync throws and existsSync is true`: mocks existsSync→true and statSync→EIO, runs `runRuleOnCode("// @story docs/stories/fs-stat-io-error.story.md")`, asserts presence of `fileAccessError` diagnostics and that the embedded `error` string contains "EIO". - `[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] rule reports fileAccessError when fs throws`: mocks both existsSync and statSync to throw EACCES and confirms `fileAccessError` diagnostics include "EACCES". - Helper `runRuleOnCode` builds a fake ESLint context with `report` capturing, `getSourceCode().getAllComments()` returning the `@story` line, and invokes the rule’s `Program` listener to collect diagnostics, validating rule behavior without full ESLint runtime.

traceability.notes: Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION is fully implemented. The `traceability/valid-story-reference` ESLint rule and its supporting utilities enforce that `@story` annotations reference real, accessible `.story.md` files, stay within project boundaries, and adhere to configurable resolution rules. Security requirements are met via rejection of unsafe absolute/traversal paths, and existence checks are cached and wrapped in robust error handling that reports clear diagnostics (`fileMissing`, `invalidExtension`, `invalidPath`, `fileAccessError`) instead of throwing. Configuration options (`storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, `requireStoryExtension`) are implemented and thoroughly covered by RuleTester and Jest tests, which also validate filesystem error scenarios and project boundary behavior, including misconfigured directories outside the project root. Documentation in `docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md` clearly describes path resolution, boundary rules, error messages, and configuration with examples. Targeted tests for `tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts` execute without reported failures, providing concrete evidence that all acceptance criteria and enumerated requirements for this story are satisfied.
